cohort: 687 pregnant Chinese women in their first trimester
finding: Pregnant women with higher levels of physical activity self-efficacy and social support had lower odds of not meeting physical activity guidelines, while younger age, lower education, primiparity, uncertainty about delivery mode, and higher levels of pregnancy-associated discomfort were associated with higher odds of not meeting the guidelines.
mod_finding: Women who were unsure of their delivery mode had higher odds of not meeting physical activity guidelines (aOR = 2.32; 95% CI: 1.95-5.64).
